messages:
maya: Heads-up — after last night's driver roll (535.86 -> 535.113) we're seeing intermittent P2P failures on mixed A100v1/A100v2 nodes in gpu-us-west2. Several training pods dropped to NET fallback and throughput tanked.

deploy-bot: driver-roll completed on pool 'gpu-us-west2' at 2024-11-02T03:12Z. 80 nodes patched, 20 left pending (canaries).

sam: Symptoms? repro steps?

maya: Short version: distributed jobs stuck or much slower. NCCL logs show repeated P2P errors and then sockets used instead. Example from one pod: 
```
[0] NCCL WARN NET/Socket : Using TCP for transports (no direct P2P)
[0] NCCL WARN P2P : P2P route not found between rank 0 and 1
[0] NCCL INFO Setting process to use sockets for ring
```

ravi: Can you paste `nvidia-smi topo -m` and `dmesg | grep -i nvlink` from an affected node?

maya: Pasted outputs from node gpu-usw2-12: 
```
$ nvidia-smi topo -m
        GPU0    GPU1    CPU
GPU0     X      NV2     NODE
GPU1    NV2      X      NODE

$ dmesg | grep -i nvlink
[  12.345678] nvidia: nvlink: probing link 1 failed: -5
[  12.345680] nvidia: p2p: link init failed for GPU1
[  12.345682] nvidia: module: firmware mismatch: nvlink fw 1.2.0 != kernel expected 1.1.8
```

leo: interesting — firmware mismatch + mixed SKU. We rolled drivers but didn't coordinate nvlink firmware upgrade on some hosts. That explains P2P flapping across v1/v2 pairs.

sam: How widespread?

deploy-bot: Fleet scan shows ~23% of gpu-us-west2 nodes report nvlink fw 1.1.8 and 66% report 1.2.0; mixed on ~11 nodes that host both v1 and v2 GPUs (PCI topology differences).

ravi: Temporary mitigation: set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 for scheduling group or per-job env. That forces sockets and prevents stalls while we fix firmware. Not ideal for perf but safe.

maya: Confirmed: exporting NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 prevents the P2P error cascade, jobs continue albeit ~2.3x slower for all-reduce. We'll use as short-term stopgap.

leo: Longer term plan:
- Canary rollback of driver on the latest patched nodes (owner: leo) back to 535.86 to see if nvlink behavior stabilizes.
- Coordinate nvlink firmware updates with host vendor to push uniform firmware 1.2.0 (owner: maya / infra-eng).
- Add node label `nvlink-unreliable=true` and an affinity rule so scheduler avoids mixing GPUs from labeled nodes in the same NCCL job (owner: ravi).

ravi: Commands I'll run: 
```
kubectl label node gpu-usw2-12 nvlink-unreliable=true --overwrite
# patch DaemonSet to inject NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 into MPI job pods as a stopgap
```

sam: Also add a perf regression alert: if NCCL all-reduce tail latency > 2x baseline for a job group, page on-call.

ci-bot: Created ticket INC-3921 in infra (nvlink p2p regressions after driver roll), assigned to maya. Linked to telemetry dashboard: https://grafana.company.internal/d/abcd/nccl-p2p-fallbacks

maya: I'll coordinate with vendor on firmware flash schedule. For immediate action:
- Ravi: label nodes and update admission webhook to prefer non-labeled nodes for P2P group placement.
- Leo: start canary rollback on 5 recently-upgraded nodes and gather `nvidia-smi topo -m` + `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version` before/after.

leo: starting rollback job now. I'll post diffs.

ravi: I'll also add a quick node check script to the preflight for driver upgrades: `dmesg | grep -i nvlink` and `modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic` and fail the upgrade if firmware+kernel/driver mismatch detected.

maya: Good. Let's avoid a full fleet re-roll until firmware coordination confirmed. We'll keep NCCL_P2P_DISABLE as a temporary flag for new job templates.

sam: Thanks — keep updates here. If we see deadlocks instead of just performance loss, escalate immediately.

leo: Update: after rollback on 5 nodes, 4/5 show stable NV2 topology and no nvlink dmesg errors. One node still noisy — vendor support ticket opened.

maya: Filing postmortem checklist and follow-ups in INC-3921.

ci-bot: Monitoring alert created to watch % of nodes with mixed nvlink fw per pool, threshold 5% -> pager.
